Education / Colleges & universities

From application season to alumni, without the paperwork chase

Colleges and universities juggle thousands of applicants, many programs, counseling rounds, hostels and student services. We connect the admissions CRM, college ERP and student channels so applicants know what is missing, students get handbook answers at any hour, and grievances, ragging reports and distress reach the right committee or counselor.

The challenge

What makes colleges & universities different.

01

Applicants submit incomplete or unreadable documents across several counseling rounds, and admissions staff chase them one call at a time.

02

Withdrawals and refunds have to follow the UGC fee refund policy, and original certificates may be verified and returned but never retained.

03

The same questions about hostel rules, exam forms, scholarships and timetables reach department offices hundreds of times a term.

04

Grievances, ragging complaints and signs of distress need a fast, recorded route to the right committee or counselor, not a shared inbox.

05

Alumni records go stale after graduation, so mentoring, placements and giving depend on a few personal networks.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for colleges & universities.

01

Program-wise enquiry routing

Enquiries tagged by program, campus and entrance exam, assigned to the right counselor and followed up with approved content through each counseling round.

02

Document checklist and verification queue

Program and category checklists, readability and name-match checks on uploads, and a verification queue for the admissions office, with originals verified in person and returned the same day.

03

Handbook and policy helpdesk

Students and parents ask about hostel rules, exam forms, scholarships and fees and get answers cited from the current handbook, with anything personal or sensitive handed to staff.

04

Committee-routed concerns

Grievances go to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee channel, ragging reports to the Anti-Ragging Committee with the national helpline shown, and distress to the counseling center.

05

Semester results and grade cards

Grade cards released behind secure links once the examination controller publishes results, with revaluation and supplementary exam windows in the same notice.

06

Alumni network and mentoring

An opt-in alumni directory, annual profile refresh, event invitations by batch and city, and mentor matches between alumni and current students approved by the alumni office.

Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus tours

Enquiries from ads, the website, fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp land in one CRM with their source, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and move to a campus tour or open-day slot with reminders and post-visit follow-up.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

In admission season, enquiries arrive faster than the front office can return calls. Leads sit in counselors' personal phones and spreadsheets, families who asked for a tour never get a slot, and the institution cannot tell which campaign or fair produced confirmed admissions.

Trigger

A parent or applicant submits a Meta or Google lead form or the website form, scans a fair or walk-in QR code, or messages the admissions WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Create or update one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with source, campaign, grade or program, campus, and the consent and notice version shown on the form.
  • Send an approved WhatsApp acknowledgment with the prospectus link and the counselor's name, assigned by grade or program, campus and preferred language.
  • Answer common questions on fees, transport, dates and eligibility only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule; route anything else to the counselor with a short summary.
  • Offer campus tour and open-day slots from the admissions calendar, share directions and a visitor pass for the gate, and remind the family the day before with a one-tap reschedule.
  • After the visit, prompt the counselor to record the outcome and send the registration or application link the family asked for.
  • Escalate enquiries with no counselor contact within the agreed time to the admissions head, and report enquiries, tours and admissions by source each morning.

Human checkpoint

Counselors make every follow-up call and record outcomes, and the admissions head approves templates, answer content and assignment rules. The workflow never screens or ranks children or parents, and seats under RTE Section 12(1)(c) follow the state's own portal and process.

Apply and enrollAdvanced5–7 weeks

Applications, document checklists and verification for colleges

Applicants complete one form with a program and category checklist. Uploads are checked for completeness, readability and name or date mismatches, the admissions office verifies each file in a queue, and missing items trigger reminders until the seat is confirmed.

Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Applications arrive across counseling rounds with missing marksheets, blurred category certificates and names that differ between documents. Staff chase applicants by phone, originals are sometimes kept against the rules, and seats stay unconfirmed while the next round approaches.

Trigger

An applicant submits the online application, or the admissions office opens a counseling round and invites shortlisted applicants to complete their documents.

How it runs

  • Show the checklist for the chosen program and category, such as marksheets, entrance scorecard, transfer and migration certificates, and category or disability certificates.
  • Check each upload for type, readability and completeness, and extract name, date of birth and marks as a draft to compare across documents.
  • Place each file in the admissions office queue with mismatches and unreadable pages highlighted beside the original images.
  • Send polite reminders for missing or rejected items with the reason and deadline, and stop reminders once the file is complete.
  • Collect the anti-ragging undertaking reference number and the APAAR or ABC ID where applicable, and book an in-person slot to verify and return original certificates.
  • On approval, send the offer and fee link, write the confirmed student to the college ERP and update seat counts by program and category.

Human checkpoint

Admissions officers verify every document and decide eligibility, category and seat allocation; extraction only drafts. Originals are verified in person and returned at once, as UGC requires, and withdrawals and refunds follow the UGC fee refund policy with the registrar's approval.

Attend and learnStandard4–5 weeks

Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbook

Students, parents and online learners ask questions on WhatsApp, the portal or the app and get answers cited from the current handbook, fee policy, academic calendar or help center. Grievances, ragging reports and signs of distress go straight to people.

Colleges & universities · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Department offices and support teams answer the same questions about exam forms, hostel rules, scholarships, certificates and refunds all term. Answers vary by who replies, and serious messages about harassment, ragging or distress can sit in the same inbox as routine queries.

Trigger

A student, parent or learner sends a question to the helpdesk WhatsApp number, the student portal or the in-app help widget.

How it runs

  • Screen every message first for ragging, harassment, self-harm or emergency words agreed with the owner; on a match, alert the named person at once and show the national anti-ragging helpline or Tele-MANAS, 14416.
  • Classify the rest into topics such as exams, fees, hostel, scholarships, certificates, login or refunds.
  • Answer only from the approved handbook, policy and help center documents, citing the section used; low-confidence answers are not sent.
  • Hand grievances to the institution's grievance channel, account-specific requests to the right office, and anything unanswered to a staffed queue with a summary.
  • Flag questions the documents could not answer so owners can update them, and re-index changed documents the same day.

Human checkpoint

The dean of students or learner success lead owns the sensitive-message rules and the staffed queue. Ragging reports go to the Anti-Ragging Committee and grievances to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee; fee waivers, discipline and academic exceptions are decided only by the authorized office.

Assess and reportStandard3–4 weeks

Report cards and results released securely to families

Once the principal or examination controller locks results, each report card or grade card is generated and the parent or adult student is notified with a secure, expiring link. PTM booking or revaluation options follow in the same notice.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Report cards are printed, signed and handed out on one crowded day, or forwarded as PDFs in groups where they can reach the wrong family. Corrections after release are messy, and colleges field calls about grade cards, revaluation windows and supplementary exams.

Trigger

The principal or examination controller marks results as final in the ERP or examination system for a class, program or semester.

How it runs

  • Generate each student's report or grade card from the locked results using the approved template and the remarks teachers entered.
  • Check for missing marks, unapproved remarks or records the exam office has flagged, and hold those until the exam office clears them.
  • Notify the parent or adult student with an approved template and a secure link that opens after a one-time code, never the document in chat.
  • Include the PTM booking link for schools, or revaluation and supplementary exam windows and fees for colleges.
  • Log every open, resend on request, and point families to DigiLocker where the board or university issues documents through it.

Human checkpoint

The principal or examination controller locks results and approves release, and teachers own their remarks. Revaluation, grace marks and any hold on a result are decided only by the examination office under the institution's rules, never by the workflow.

Pay, renew and stay connectedStarter2–3 weeks

Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts

Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Accounts staff chase dues by phone, reminders sometimes reach the wrong parent or a class group, and children can be embarrassed when dues are raised in class. Installment and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts, and receipts are issued by hand.

Trigger

A fee installment approaches or passes its due date in the ERP fee ledger, a payment succeeds or fails at the gateway, or a fee payer asks about fees.

How it runs

  • Read due dates, amounts and concessions from the ERP fee ledger and send an approved reminder to the registered fee payer a set number of days before the due date.
  • Include a payment link for UPI, cards and net banking, and post successful payments to the ledger with an instant receipt, or a GST invoice where the fee is taxable.
  • After the due date, send no more than the agreed number of courteous reminders, each with an option to request an installment plan or speak to accounts.
  • Route installment, concession, scholarship and refund requests to the accounts officer with the student's ledger summary and the applicable refund policy.
  • Give accounts a daily view of dues, promises to pay and failed payments, with no list shared with teachers or classes.

Human checkpoint

The accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.

Pay, renew and stay connectedStarter2–4 weeks

Alumni directory, events and mentoring

Graduating students opt in to the alumni network, profiles are refreshed by a short annual form, event invitations go to relevant batches and cities, and mentor matches between alumni and current students are approved by the alumni office.

Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Alumni records go stale within a few years of graduation, invitations go to dead email addresses, and mentoring and placement referrals depend on a few personal networks. Reunions and giving drives are organized from scratch each time.

Trigger

A student graduates and is invited to join, an annual profile refresh falls due, or the alumni office schedules an event, mentoring round or giving campaign.

How it runs

  • Invite graduating students to opt in with a consent screen that states how their details will be used and what other alumni can see.
  • Send an annual refresh form for employer, city and mentoring interests, and mark records that bounce or stay unconfirmed.
  • Segment invitations by batch, program and city, and track registrations and attendance for each event.
  • Suggest mentor matches between opted-in alumni and current students by field and interest, for the alumni office to approve and introduce.
  • Report profile freshness, event attendance and mentoring activity, and acknowledge every gift with a receipt from the accounts office.

Human checkpoint

The alumni relations officer approves every campaign, introduction and mentor match, and current students choose whether to accept a mentor. Directory details are shown to other alumni only where each person chose to share them.
